answers.children: Gordon Setters are reasonably good with children. Their large size and energetic nature mean they can knock over small children with an excited tail wag during play, yet their loyal and gentle temperament allows them to form close bonds with family youngsters when given space to move. The breed's hunting background gives it stamina that suits active games but requires supervision to prevent boisterous accidents. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 7/10)
answers.other-pets: Gordon Setters can get along with other pets when raised together. Their bird-hunting instincts create a moderate prey drive that may lead to chasing smaller animals, while their energetic build and loyalty to family sometimes produce tension with unfamiliar dogs of the same sex. The long silky coat and intelligent nature help them adapt to multi-pet homes with proper introductions.
answers.exercise: Gordon Setters need at least one to two hours of vigorous daily exercise. Without this outlet their high energy leads to destructiveness such as chewing shoes or digging in gardens, reflecting their Scottish origins as hunters that covered rough Highland terrain for hours. Long hikes, runs and field work suit their stamina and pointing instincts best.
answers.shedding: Yes — Gordon Setters shed moderately year-round, with heavier seasonal sheds. Their long silky coat with feathering on the legs and tail tangles easily and traps loose hair around the home, demanding regular attention to prevent mats especially behind the ears and under the belly where the flowing black-and-tan hair is thickest. (PawLabs shedding score: 6/10)
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is truly hypoallergenic, and the Gordon Setter is not one commonly suggested for allergy sufferers. The long silky coat with its feathering and undercoat sheds moderate amounts of hair and dander that can trigger reactions, while the breed's energetic hunting background means it spends time outdoors collecting pollen and debris that further affects sensitive individuals.
answers.training: Gordon Setters are moderately easy to train. Their intelligence and exceptional hunting instincts make them highly responsive to purposeful work such as pointing and retrieving, yet a stubborn streak rooted in their independent Scottish field heritage can surface if the approach lacks firmness and consistency, requiring an owner who channels their loyalty effectively.
answers.lifespan: Gordon Setters live 10-12 years. Their large athletic build developed for stamina in the Scottish Highlands supports an active life, though the breed's health robustness is only average and specific health issues can appear that affect longevity in some lines.
answers.size: Gordon Setters reach 45-80 lb and stand 23-27 in tall. The substantial, muscular frame built for covering rugged terrain feels imposing indoors yet graceful when moving, with the long silky coat adding visual bulk that makes the dog seem even larger during its energetic daily circuits of the house and garden.
answers.barking: Gordon Setters bark moderately. Bred as bird hunters and pointers in Scotland they remain relatively quiet while focused on scent work but will alert with purposeful barks when something unusual enters their territory, their loyal temperament prompting them to guard the family without excessive noise once the threat is assessed.
answers.apartment: Gordon Setters do not suit apartment living well. Their high energy and need for at least one to two hours of vigorous daily exercise mean they struggle to settle indoors without becoming destructive, while the large muscular build and long silky coat that sheds moderately create additional challenges in confined spaces lacking room to move.
answers.first-time: Gordon Setters are not ideal as a first dog. Their high energy that quickly turns destructive without sufficient exercise, combined with a stubborn streak during training and the grooming demands of the long silky coat, place demands on time and consistency that can overwhelm novices despite the breed's deep loyalty and intelligence.
